passages.note: Assembly Floor concurrence in Senate amendments, the final Assembly passage vote; Wicks is in the Ayes list and the 26 Noes are far above the 10% near-unanimous floor.
passages.tally_quote: Ayes Count 48 Noes Count 26 NVR Count 5

passages.provision_quote: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.

rows.reasoning: Wicks voted Aye on AB 1482 (2019-2020), a tenancy bill whose operative Section 1947.12 caps annual rent increases at "5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower" on units that had no cap before, which is to "Strengthen existing rent stabilization and extend coverage to more units". It is not the "all rental units communitywide" rung, because the same section exempts classes of units, including "Housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years" and owner-occupied duplexes, and it is not the "Maintain current tenant protections" rung, because it adds a cap rather than keeping the existing set. The act dates from her 2018-2022 Assembly term, the same chamber of the same legislature, so it is in-term under V5.
